title: Totalization of functorial object injective resolutions
statement: Given a functor E : C ⥤ CochainComplex C ℕ with a natural quasi-isomorphic augmentation from single₀ C, with E mapping zero morphisms to zero, E.obj 0 a zero complex, and with injective terms, there exist a functor I : Plus C ⥤ Plus C and a natural quasi-isomorphism Plus.ι C ⟶ I ⋙ Plus.ι C whose terms are injective and which preserves every strict lower bound.

proof.text: Extend each nonnegative resolution E(A) by zero to integer degrees. Identify the extension of single₀(A) with the integer single complex, obtaining a natural augmented integer resolution. Apply the zero-preserving extension functor to the original complex K degreewise using mapHomologicalComplex. The outer index p is the degree of K and the inner index q is the resolution degree; its natural augmentation comes from singleRow₀(K).

For any bound a of K, all terms with p<a or q<0 are zero. Use hasTotal_of_boundedBelow to obtain each diagonal coproduct. The canonical Mathlib total complex and total.map define a replacement functor independently of a. Compose the inverse of singleRow₀ObjTotal with the totalized augmentation; the naturality and composition identities for total.map prove its naturality.

Prove comparison for bicomplexes bounded below in both indices by truncating outer columns above x=n−b+1 when checking homology in degree n. The projection to this truncation is an isomorphism in degrees n−1,n,n+1 because any omitted term has inner degree below b. For the truncated map, transport columnwise quasi-isomorphisms along the truncation isomorphisms and apply the existing finite-column total comparison. The naturality square and the two-out-of-three property on degree-n homology prove comparison for the original map. Apply this to the augmented resolutions; extendMap preserves their quasi-isomorphisms and singleRow₀ObjTotal is an isomorphism.

In degree n, use the finite interval a≤p≤n to index all possibly nonzero diagonal terms, with q=n−p. They are injective by the hypothesis on E and extension by zero. Their finite biproduct is injective and is isomorphic to the chosen diagonal coproduct by its universal property. If n<a, every diagonal term is zero, so the coproduct identity is zero by its hom-ext principle. This proves preservation of each lower bound, including the empty diagonal case.
